blocks.content: PART A: BARTER SYSTEM – THE BEGINNING OF EXCHANGE

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The barter system relies on the direct exchange of goods and services but is severely limited by the requirement of double coincidence of wants.
Money originated to overcome limitations of barter, functioning primarily as a medium of exchange and a measure of value.
Functions of money are broadly classified into Primary, Secondary, and Contingent functions.
Secondary functions include serving as a store of value, standard of deferred payments, and transfer of value.
Modern forms of money encompass commodity money, fiat money (backed by legal tender), credit money, and plastic money.

blocks.content: 1. Meaning of Barter System (Very Detailed)

Barter system refers to the system of exchange in which goods and services were directly exchanged for other goods and services without using money. For example, a farmer exchanged rice for clothes with a weaver. This system existed in primitive societies when money had not yet developed.
2. Detailed Problems of Barter System

The barter system failed because of several serious problems:



1. Lack of Double Coincidence of Wants:

Both buyer and seller must want each other’s goods at the same time.



2. Absence of Common Measure of Value:

There was no standard unit to measure value of goods.



3. Difficulty in Storage of Wealth:

Many goods like food items were perishable.



4. Indivisibility of Goods:

Goods like cattle could not be divided into smaller units.



5. Difficulty in Deferred Payments:

Future payments were almost impossible under barter system.
PART B: ORIGIN AND MEANING OF MONEY
3. Origin of Money
Money originated as a solution to the problems of barter system. Gradually, certain commodities became commonly acceptable, which later evolved into modern money.
4. Meaning and Definition of Money (Explained Line by Line)

Money is anything that is generally accepted as a medium of exchange, measure of value, store of value and standard of deferred payments.



Generally accepted means accepted by everyone.

Medium of exchange means used to buy and sell goods.

Measure of value means used to express prices.

Store of value means saving purchasing power.

Standard of deferred payments means making future payments.
5. Characteristics of Ideal Money (In Depth)

Good money should possess the following characteristics:



• General Acceptability – accepted by all.

• Durability – lasts for long time.

• Portability – easy to carry.

• Divisibility – can be divided into small units.

• Uniformity – same value everywhere.

• Stability of Value – value should not fluctuate much.
PART C: FUNCTIONS OF MONEY – CORE OF THE CHAPTER
6. Classification of Functions of Money

Functions of money are classified into three categories:

• Primary Functions

• Secondary Functions

• Contingent Functions
7. Primary Functions of Money (Very Deep Explanation)

1. Medium of Exchange:

Money acts as an intermediary between buyer and seller. It eliminates barter and solves the problem of double coincidence of wants.



2. Measure of Value:

Money provides a common unit to express prices and compare values of goods.
8. Secondary Functions of Money (Very Deep Explanation)

Secondary functions arise from primary functions:



• Store of Value:

Money allows people to save purchasing power for future use.



• Standard of Deferred Payments:

Money enables loans and credit transactions.



• Transfer of Value:

Money helps in transferring purchasing power.

rows: Money acts as a common medium
Easy and stable to store over time

blocks.content: 9. Contingent Functions of Money (Very Deep Explanation)

Contingent functions support the credit system:



• Basis of Credit – credit depends on money.

• Liquidity of Wealth – assets can be easily converted.

• Distribution of National Income – wages, rent, interest and profit.
PART D: TYPES OF MONEY – COMPLETE COVERAGE
10. Commodity Money
Commodity money has intrinsic value. Examples include gold and silver coins.
11. Fiat Money
Fiat money is government-issued money with legal backing. It has no intrinsic value.
12. Credit Money
Credit money refers to bank-created money such as cheques and demand deposits.
13. Plastic Money

items: Primary functions of money consist specifically of Medium of Exchange and Measure of Value.
Fiat Money derives its value from government decree/order and serves as legal tender.
Lack of double coincidence of wants is the most frequently tested limitation of the Barter System.
Plastic money refers to debit cards and credit cards used in modern financial transactions.

blocks.content: Plastic money includes debit cards, credit cards and smart cards.
PART E: IMPORTANCE OF MONEY IN MODERN ECONOMY
14. Importance of Money (Explained Fully)
Money plays a crucial role in modern economy. It facilitates production, trade, capital formation, savings, investment and economic growth.
SSC ABSOLUTE FINAL REVISION POINTS

• Barter system failed due to lack of double coincidence of wants

• Money is generally accepted medium of exchange

• Medium of exchange is the most important function

• Store of value enables saving

• Fiat money has legal backing

• Credit system depends on money
